exposure: Obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome (OAPS) with standard low-dose aspirin and low-molecular-weight heparin treatment
cohort: The study included 256 OAPS patients (166 criteria OAPS, 90 non-criteria OAPS) who achieved live birth, along with 768 matched healthy controls.
finding: Despite standard treatment, OAPS patients who deliver successfully remain at an increased risk for persistent maternal hypercoagulability and anemia, and their neonates have significantly lower birth weight and elevated risks of neonatal infection and hyperbilirubinemia.
birth_weight: Neonates of treated OAPS patients had significantly lower birth weight.
gest_age: The infection risk remained significant in full-term infants, implying inclusion of full-term babies, but no specific gestational age range for the whole cohort is provided.
